title: The Effect of Substituting Water for Artificially Sweetened Beverages on Glycemic and Weight Measures in People With Type 2 Diabetes: The Study of Drinks With Artificial Sweeteners (SODAS), a Randomized Trial
authors: Odegaard AO, Chang J, Jiang L, Rashid S, Rydell S, Mitchell NR, et al.
population: Adults aged 35 years or older with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c 6.5 to 8.5% who habitually drank commercial artificially sweetened beverages; University of California, Irvine, and University of Minnesota, June 2019 to March 2023
funder: This work was supported by the National Institutes of Health National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (grant R01DK117028). The funder had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: No potential conflicts of interest relevant to this article were reported.
result: Participants were randomised to 24 oz per day of a commercial artificially sweetened beverage of their choice (n = 91) or unflavoured water (n = 90); 179 provided complete data. HbA1c changed from 7.19% to 7.14% with sweetened beverages and from 7.20% to 7.44% with water; the adjusted mean difference in change was 0.29 percentage points higher with water (SE 0.12; P = 0.013). The difference in change of fasting glucose was 4.71 mg/dL (SE 6.43; P = 0.47), and weight change was 1.11 kg higher with water (SE 0.55; P = 0.045).
